Rests on a premise about ci/delta.is_engine not verifiable from the bundle; placing the module outside l7r/ to honor 'as tooling' literally is a design choice, not a fidelity finding.

decisions.summary: Exits: 'FR-008 green: landed with its fresh rate. Red: the failing seeds recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be placed correctly ruled through make arbiter-ask (D11, D35).'
decisions.why: Template text from another feature: FR-008 is 'the engine stays in Python', not a landing condition; D11 and D35 exist nowhere in this plan or spec-cited.md; 'placed correctly' and 'fresh rate' are placement/seed-pass language for a tool that changes no stage. As written, the red exit sets T01 down on 'failing seeds'. T01 cannot make a seed regress (FR-007), so the only failing seeds at its landing are ones already failing on HEAD, and request.md 4 ('should not require all seeds to pass if seeds were previously failing') and 5 ('not have a requirement to have all of our seeds pass') exclude exactly that as a reason. It abandons the requested survey on a condition the GM ruled out: not physically necessary, not implied by the GM's words (they say the opposite), not serving the purpose. Fix: green = tests red without D1 and make perf-fanout on the current engine compared with research/fanout-2026-10-26.txt (FR-001, SC-001); red = only a seed passing on HEAD that fails after (FR-007); strike FR-008, D11, D35, 'placed correctly', 'fresh rate'.

decisions.summary: D1 prints the multiplier chains only for each stage of 300,000 calls or more at the larger size
decisions.why: SC-001 (cited in full) requires the output to list EVERY chain of 50k+ calls with its anchor, and the plan's own Performance Goals restates that, but D1's stage gate cannot reach a function called 50,000-299,999 times in a stage whose total is under 300,000: such a chain is never printed. The GM named this range himself (request.md 2: 'hundreds of thousands or millions of times'), and FR-002 scopes every engine task against this output, so a skipped chain is a hotspot no task is ever scoped against - the gate defeats the survey's purpose. Walking every stage is not impossible, the GM's words do not imply the gate, and 'kept as written there' in the design note does not override SC-001. Fix: the stage gate becomes HOT (any stage holding a non-builtin function called HOT or more times at the larger size gets its chains), or there is no stage gate; the walk itself stays as written. If the author holds that the 300,000 gate is right, that is a spec amendment of SC-001 for the GM's review, not a plan decision.

decisions.summary: JOBS defaults to 3 rather than the design note's 5, citing the shared memory cap

make perf-fanout survey tool, JOBS=3 convention, lands through make land

decisions.summary: make perf adds a separate counting pass after the timed rolls: same seeds (and sizes under SCALING=1), sys.monitoring PY_START counter on tool id 3, per-stage per-seed calls and the snapshot's versions recorded
decisions.why: Request 4: 'record call counts alongside the timings'; a separate pass keeps the timings the GM said to keep recording undistorted. FR-006 adopts call-count-flag.md; tool id is mechanism.

decisions.summary: Counts are of Python functions only; shapely/numpy C work is not counted
decisions.why: The GM adopted the session's measure ('do as you say and record call counts'); FR-006 defers to call-count-flag.md, and D1's survey counts the same Python-level calls. A definition of the metric, not a carve-out from it.

decisions.summary: Counting pass overhead measured on the reference seeds and recorded beside the code; a test rolls one stage twice and asserts equal counts
decisions.why: Enforcement of the requested gate: the GM chose counts 'because ... that is consistent'; the test only fails if they are not.

decisions.summary: perf_review.check, run by the push, compares the newest -start/-end pair's counts seed by seed and stage by stage
decisions.why: Request 4: 'that flag would replace the timing band' - the count check stands where the band check stood. The bundle does not let me confirm the band's own reach, so this is classed on the request's framing of replacement in place.

decisions.summary: A -start/-end pair on different versions (interpreter, numpy, shapely) is 'not compared', never flagged, and the push proceeds
decisions.why: Request 4: 'the call counts themselves are the thing that we are gating on', and an increase 'would need to be accepted by the arbiter'. Applying the gate to a cross-version pair is neither impossible nor purpose-defeating: it costs one arbiter call, and the arbiter can see the versions differ ('the kind of thing that I would expect the arbiter to be able to handle without me'). The carve-out resolves 'the delta cannot be attributed' by not watching at all, so any engine increase lands unwatched whenever a dependency bump sits between -start and -end. Should say: a pair on different versions is not compared AND the push refuses until a comparable pair exists (the -start re-rolled on the current versions) or the arbiter rules on it under the same <NNN>-calls subject - never a silent pass.

decisions.summary: The line: over 5% in any stage on any seed (CALLS_STAGE_LINE) or 2% in the total (CALLS_TOTAL_LINE), GUESS knobs with the reason beside them
decisions.why: The GM: the count flag 'would replace the timing band' and arbiter attention 'if it is increasing by too much'; FR-006 and SC-005 say 'over the line'. Values are labeled knobs, not measured claims.

decisions.summary: Over-the-line increase with no arbiter accept refuses the push and names make arbiter-ask SUBJECT=<NNN>-calls with stages, seeds, counts; an accept in arbiter.jsonl clears it; a decrease is printed and needs nothing
decisions.why: Request 4 ('would need to be accepted by the arbiter'); FR-006; SC-005 (refuses and names the arbiter command; accepted lands with the ruling recorded).

decisions.summary: Timings printed for information only; no rule acts on them; the band FLAG retired, perf_bands keeps only what printing needs
decisions.why: Request 4: 'keep recording the timings, but completely stop using timings as a gate on anything'; SC-005.

decisions.summary: scripts/sync-with-main.sh refuses on the check's exit as it refuses on its failing to run
decisions.why: Enforcement of the requested gate on the push path (FR-006 'the push check'); no reach beyond the call-count check itself.

decisions.summary: Round arbiter's agent file gains the call-count case: accept when the cost of a rule the feature adds and commensurate, continue to optimize first, to the GM when too large
decisions.why: Request 4: accepted by the arbiter 'and possibly raised to my attention if it is increasing by too much'; FR-006 names the arbiter's agent file.

decisions.why: Request 5: the survey and the call-count watch first (US1, US5); request 4; FR-006.

decisions.why: Request 4 and 5; FR-006, SC-005. Its exits test the requested gate. Its ruling stands on D3, whose versions carve-out is ruled separately.

decisions.summary: analysis tested on synthetic pstats data, profiling seam stubbed; a tools/CLAUDE.md row

decisions.summary: only Python-level function calls are counted; shapely and numpy C work is not
decisions.why: The GM's concern is Python functions called hundreds of thousands or millions of times (request 2), and FR-006 adopts call-count-flag.md, which wants exactly this. It is the measure asked for, not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: pass overhead measured and recorded; a test asserts equal counts on two rolls of one stage
decisions.why: Checks that the requested counts are deterministic, which is the GM's stated reason for gating on them; enforcement, not scope.

decisions.summary: perf_review.check compares the newest -start/-end pair's counts seed by seed and stage by stage
decisions.why: FR-006 / SC-005: call counts are what is watched.

decisions.summary: CHANGED: a pair on different interpreter/library versions is not compared and REFUSES the push until a comparable pair (the -start re-taken) exists or the round arbiter rules on the <NNN>-calls subject; it never passes silently
decisions.why: The earlier text let a version-mismatched pair pass unflagged, a hole through which an increase could land without the arbiter (FR-006: an increase over the line 'owes the round arbiter's acceptance before it lands'). The new text closes it: nothing passes unexamined, and the way out is the arbiter or a comparable measurement, as the GM wanted (request 4: 'accepted by the arbiter ... the kind of thing that I would expect the arbiter to be able to handle without me'). It is enforcement of the requested watch, not a narrowing and not new behavior beyond it.

decisions.summary: Homestead-parts family covers the 'Homestead seating' chains plus R4 (household_reach) and R8 (capacity.field_distances), sent with this family by US4.
decisions.why: request.md 5 names homestead parts as the first pairwise family outside the lanes; the block cites US4 for carrying R4 and R8 here. Nothing named in the research is dropped.

decisions.summary: After T06, before ground cover; re-scoped first by make perf-fanout STAGES=homesteads on the then-current engine.
decisions.why: Order is request.md 5's (homestead parts, then ground cover). Re-survey before change is FR-002.

decisions.summary: Green: each named chain falls at least tenfold, cohort no regression, claims clean; red: set down, cannot-be-done claim to arbiter-ask; one landing per map-neutral chain group, cohort judging any that moves maps.
decisions.why: Tenfold per chain is at least as strict as SC-002; cohort and claims are FR-007/FR-004; identical manifests where free and per-seed comparison for deliberate changes is the GM-approved approach (request.md 5). Setting a task down leaves the feature open, which narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: R8, which shows no chain, is measured by stage time and field_distances share at seed 47, 40 households, before/after as a seed-by-seed A/B against HEAD plus a pool reroll diffed against HEAD's manifests; reported, gating nothing.
decisions.why: This is FR-003's rule for a chainless task word for word (stage time at the finding's seed and size, before and after, A/B against HEAD). 'Gating nothing' is FR-006 (timings flag nothing). The table names make perf-profile as the tool; the prose binds it to an A/B against HEAD, and the stage time has to come from that A/B, not from cProfile seconds. Seed 47 is taken as the seed R8 names; the bundle does not carry R8's text.

decisions.summary: Ground-cover family (close_belt_gaps, household_bamboo->stand_spares_seats, belt.fouled, convex_hull, belt_law, _crown_seat_clear, grove and hinterland genexprs), after homestead parts and before water.
decisions.why: request.md 5: ground cover follows homestead parts, and both come before the lanes. Putting water (outside the lanes) after ground cover is consistent with that.

decisions.summary: Re-scope by make perf-fanout STAGES=hinterland,windbreak, keeping the chains that still stand after T04/T07.
decisions.why: FR-002. The ruling assumes, as the block does, that every chain step 3 names (including the grove genexprs and close_belt_gaps) runs inside the hinterland or windbreak stages. The bundle carries no stage names and the manifest forbids repository reads, so that premise is unverified here. If any named chain runs in another stage, this filter drops it with no before/after count, and STAGES must be widened. The green exit, 'each chain named', still holds the task to step 3's full list.

decisions.summary: Tenfold per chain, cohort, claims; one landing per chain group.
decisions.why: Same exits as T07; FR-003/FR-004/FR-007.

decisions.summary: Field settle (R7) and the water chains (brook_rules.crosses_mid_run, partition.keep_rows), using the fabric's existing STRtree; after ground cover, before the lanes; one landing.
decisions.why: Outside the lanes, so before them per request.md 5; US4 carries R7 with its family. One landing is a budget, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: Re-scope by make perf-fanout STAGES=field only.
decisions.why: FR-002. The ruling assumes the brook and partition chains run inside the field stage. The bundle does not settle this. If the brook chains run in a stage of their own, STAGES=field misses them, and the filter must name that stage too. The green exit still names every chain in step 3.

decisions.summary: Lane web and lane law converted last, started only once feature 417's lane conversions land, re-surveyed on 417's engine; the task holds 427 open until then.
decisions.why: Verbatim the approved order in request.md 5 ('the lane web and the lane law (part of US4) last, after feature 417's lane conversions, since 417 restructures that code'). Holding the feature open narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Tenfold per chain, cohort, claims; one landing per chain group.
decisions.why: Same exits as the other families.

decisions.summary: Green only when SC-002 and SC-003 are met; a missed criterion is red; an intermediate checkpoint does not close the feature.
decisions.why: Matches SC-002/SC-003 as written, including SC-003's sentence on checkpoints. The earlier wording ('stated met or not') was the narrowing, and it has been removed. SC-004 is enforced at every landing (cohort-landing in make land plus the family tasks' claims exits), and SC-005 lands with US5, so leaving them out of this exit narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: FR-005's seed-by-seed A/B against HEAD is carried out as the -end bookend's per-seed rows compared with the -start bookend's (make perf-review), not as a separate A/B run.
decisions.why: FR-005 names two instruments joined by 'and': bookends (427-start|end) AND a seed-by-seed A/B against HEAD. T11's step 9 prose claims both ('compared seed by seed against HEAD'), but its table puts the bookend pair, read per seed, under the A/B row. That reduces two instruments to one. The two are not alike. The bookends are separate runs taken days or weeks apart on a shared container, and request.md 4 names exactly that as the reason timings mislead ('which processor we were using and what the current system load is really throws them off'). An A/B runs both engines, seed by seed, in the same run, which controls for that. Nothing makes a real A/B impossible: run the pre-feature engine (the 427-start commit) against the end engine at the same seeds in one session. This is not implied by the GM's words, and it weakens the purpose of FR-005, which is a timing conclusion that load does not distort. Fix: keep the bookend pair, and add a separate seed-by-seed A/B of the 427-start commit against the end commit (each stage of each completing seed), named by its command in the table.

decisions.summary: T07 re-scopes the homestead-parts family with `make perf-fanout STAGES=homesteads` only (item 4 and the table)
decisions.why: FR-002 scopes the task list against the survey's output and request.md 5 assigns work by FAMILY (homestead parts), not by stage. A stage filter scopes by stage: any chain of this family (yards' _filled_lattice, gap_ways.way_out/trace, wood_share, R4 household_reach) that runs outside the `homesteads` stage is invisible to the re-scope and falls into no task. The block gives no reason the family is confined to that stage, and the same plan, in T08 and T09, drops the stage filter for exactly this reason ('so a chain in another stage is not dropped'). Not impossible (the unfiltered survey is used two blocks later), not implied by the GM's words, and the literal rule defeats nothing. Fix: `make perf-fanout` over every stage, as T08/T09, in item 4 and the table.

decisions.summary: R8 (field_distances, no chain) measured by an A/B of HEAD against the change in two detached worktrees, back to back, alternated, at seed 47 / 40 households, reported and gating nothing
decisions.why: FR-003 asks exactly this for a chainless finding (stage time at its seed and size, before and after, seed-by-seed A/B against HEAD); 'gating nothing' is FR-006.

decisions.summary: One landing per chain group that changes no map; the cohort judges any that does
decisions.why: Mechanics of landing; FR-007's cohort still judges every map change.

decisions.summary: T08 re-scopes with `make perf-fanout` over every stage instead of STAGES=hinterland,windbreak
decisions.why: Widens the re-scope to the whole survey FR-002 names; the family scope (ground cover, request.md 5) is unchanged.

decisions.summary: T09 re-scopes with `make perf-fanout` over every stage instead of STAGES=field
decisions.why: As T08: the full survey FR-002 names; the water/field-settle family scope is unchanged.

decisions.summary: T10 (unchanged since its BLOCKED verdict) re-scopes the lane web AND the lane law with `make perf-fanout STAGES=web` only
decisions.why: request.md 5 puts 'the lane web and the lane law' in this last task. The research section the block cites is headed 'The lane web (stage `web`) and the lane law' - a stage is named for the web, not for the law. A survey confined to stage `web` cannot see lane-law chains in any other stage, and those then land in no task at all (T07-T09 are scoped to other families). Not impossible (T08/T09 of this plan already use the unfiltered survey), not implied by the GM, and the general rule defeats nothing. Fix: `make perf-fanout` over every stage, on the engine 417 leaves, in item 4 and the table.

decisions.summary: T10 starts only after feature 417's lane conversions land, holding 427 open until then
decisions.why: The order the GM approved verbatim in request.md 5 ('the lane web and the lane law ... last, after feature 417's lane conversions').

decisions.summary: The success A/B is two detached worktrees at the 427-start commit (1cc4066ac) and the end commit, `make perf SCALING=1` back to back, alternated, every stage of every completing seed compared seed by seed; never medians or bookends alone
decisions.why: FR-005's seed-by-seed A/B against HEAD (HEAD is the end commit when T11 runs); 'never bookends alone' is stricter than FR-005, not narrower, and answers the GM's request.md 4 concern about load and processor.

decisions.summary: 417's failing seeds re-measured on the end engine with `make cohort`, recorded in 417's directory, before 417 resumes
decisions.why: request.md 5 verbatim: '417's failing seeds re-measured after 427, before 417 resumes'.

decisions.summary: Green needs SC-002 and SC-003 met and the report written; any criterion missed is red; an intermediate checkpoint does not close the feature
decisions.why: Restates SC-002/SC-003 and SC-003's own checkpoint clause; a red exit ruled by the arbiter does not close the feature green.

decisions.summary: the round arbiter accepted the plan as it stands
R4 (household_reach) moves out of T07 into its own task T12; T07 keeps the yards/gap_ways/wood_share chains and R8.
decisions.why: R4 is moved, not dropped: T12 carries it with the same tenfold exit, still in the homestead family US4 sends it with, and still ordered before the ground cover family as the GM's order (request.md 5) requires. T07's other exits, R8 test and measurements are unchanged from its CLEAR text.

decisions.summary: T12 keeps a homestead's parts rolled at the seat offered and rejects R4's research direction (one envelope per lot and size), which is the household-keyed roll feature 297 withdrew.
decisions.why: The request asks for far fewer calls computing the same thing (request.md 1, 5: 'a refactor meant to compute the same thing'; T12 goal 'the same homesteads seated'). Declining one candidate mechanism that would change what is seated, and that was already withdrawn by feature 297, narrows no clause of the request; the target (R4's chain at least tenfold down) is kept in full.

decisions.summary: T12 runs after T07, before the ground cover family.
decisions.why: Matches the GM-approved order: homestead parts, then ground cover, lanes last after 417.

decisions.summary: Green exit: R4's chain at least tenfold down, cohort with no seed regressed, claims round clean; red exit to the arbiter; one landing; measured by make perf-fanout before/after and maps-moved, re-scoped by perf-fanout first.
decisions.why: Carries US4's tenfold test, FR-002, FR-003, FR-004 and FR-007 as written; no timing gates (FR-006); nothing narrowed.

decisions.summary: T11 runs last, after every family task
decisions.why: The feature's closing measurement can only follow the work it measures; request.md 5's order (survey and watch first, lanes last) is not changed by putting the final measurement after all of it.

decisions.summary: Green only when SC-002 and SC-003 are met by the end measurement and the report is written; any criterion missed is red; an intermediate checkpoint does not close the feature; red sets the task down and a claim of impossibility goes to make arbiter-ask
decisions.why: Carries SC-002 and SC-003 at full strength, which carry request.md 1 ('literal order of magnitude', 'every single stage ... a fraction of a second ... such as 40'), and keeps SC-003's rule that an intermediate checkpoint does not close the feature. It relaxes nothing. The arbiter route for a can't-be-done claim is the project's standing escalation path, not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: The seed-by-seed A/B compares a detached worktree at the 427-start bookend commit (1cc4066ac) with one at the end commit, make perf SCALING=1 alternated start, end, start, end in one session, every stage of every completing seed compared seed by seed
decisions.why: FR-005 asks for bookends plus a seed-by-seed A/B, never medians alone. By the time the feature closes, HEAD is the end commit, so the only A/B that measures the feature's effect is against the pre-feature engine. Alternating the runs inside one session answers the GM's own point in request.md 4 that load and processor throw timings off. Comparing completing seeds only follows request.md 4 and 5 (seeds that already failed are not required to pass).

decisions.summary: Call totals for SC-002 are taken with make perf-fanout
decisions.why: SC-002 is a count of calls and the plan measures it with the feature's own call-count tool. Nothing is narrowed: the 2.5M / 6.5M targets in SC-002 still stand.

decisions.why: This is request.md 5's approved approach, word for word: '417's failing seeds re-measured after 427, before 417 resumes'.
